posts.raw_content:
🚨 MINNEAPOLIS 911 — OVERNIGHT DISPATCH

Saturday–Sunday, November 14–15
5:00 AM – 5:20 AM | 909 incidents | 683 POLICE · 191 FIRE · 35 BCR 

📍 Map attached. All data sourced from Minneapolis 911 dispatch.

· · ·

Eighteen deaths in twelve days and the count is still rising. At 7:37 this morning, dispatch logged another body in Marcy Holmes, four units. That brings the confirmed total since November 3 to at least nineteen dead across Minneapolis. Whittier logged two. Longfellow. Folwell. Audubon Park. Lyndale. Loring Park. Como. Regina. Webber-Camden. South Uptown. Hawthorne. Windom. Midtown Phillips. Hiawatha. Now Marcy Holmes. A rape was reported in Seward at 3:18 a.m., two units, the third sexual assault in that corridor in under a week. An officer emergency in Mid-City Industrial at 11:15 p.m. brought 19 units screaming to the scene, the largest single response of the night. A domestic with weapons in Logan Park at 11:18 p.m. drew six units. Structure fire in Whittier at 1:39 p.m., twelve units. Between 5 a.m. Friday and 5:20 a.m. Saturday, 909 total 911 calls flooded dispatch. Precinct 3 led again with 250. Downtown West logged 89 incidents, more than double any other neighborhood.

The guns started in East Phillips at 8:30 p.m. and did not stop. Gunshot sensors detected shots there, four units. A person with a gun call in Prospect Park at 12:17 p.m. brought seven units. Another person with a gun in Phillips West at 9:33 p.m., three units. Person with a weapon in Hawthorne at 5:33 p.m., six units. The gunfire reports clustered tight. Four calls involving firearms or gunshot sensors in a single overnight window. Hawthorne and Phillips logged gun calls for the second consecutive day. This is what a city sounds like when the shooting never stops.

The week in full. Fifteen deaths in seven days before this window even started. Whittier, Longfellow, Folwell, Audubon Park, Lyndale, Loring Park, Como, Regina, Webber-Camden, South Uptown, one by one. Five confirmed shooting dispatches. Fifty-three shots-fired and gunshot-sensor calls. Jordan alone logged seven gunfire detections. Hawthorne logged four. Eighteen rapes and sexual assaults reported across the city in seven days. Downtown West logged two. Marcy Holmes logged two. Ten robberies and carjackings. Seventy-nine auto theft calls. Whittier, Cedar Riverside, Hawthorne, Lyndale, Midtown Phillips, every one of them appearing in multiple violence categories. Six officer emergencies in seven days. Near-North. Cedar-Isles-Dean. Loring Park. South Uptown. This is not a crime spike. This is sustained, neighborhood-by-neighborhood violence grinding through the city for two straight weeks.

We have filed records requests on every death since November 3. We have sent press inquiries to the Minneapolis Police Department, the Mayor's office, and the Hennepin County Medical Examiner. Zero responses. We do not know if any of these nineteen deaths are homicides. We do not know if they are connected. We do not know why rapes are clustering in Marcy Holmes and Seward. We do not know what happened in the officer emergency in Mid-City Industrial that required 19 units. The city is not saying. The silence is the story now.

· · ·

🔴 OFFICER EMERGENCY — Mid - City Industrial, low block of Godward St Ne | 11:15 PM

Police responded to an officer emergency on the low block of Godward Street NE in Mid-City Industrial at 11:15 PM with 19 units responding. MPD has not released additional details.

· · ·

🔴 DEATH — Marcy Holmes, 800 block of 4th St Se | 7:37 AM

Four police units responded to a death call on the 800 block of 4th Street Southeast in the Marcy Holmes neighborhood at 7:37 AM Saturday. The neighborhood near the University of Minnesota campus has seen a wave of violence this week, including two sexual assault reports on Thursday, an officer emergency on Tuesday, and a domestic call involving weapons on Sunday. MPD has not released further details.

· · ·

🔴 RAPE / SEXUAL ASSAULT — Seward, Census Block Group 106200-2 | 3:18 AM

Police responded to a sexual assault call in Seward at 3:18 AM, with two units dispatched to a location in Census Block Group 106200-2. This is the second reported sexual assault in the neighborhood this week, following a call at the same census block group early Wednesday morning. MPD has not released further details about the incident.

· · ·

🔴 PERSON WITH GUN — Prospect Park - East River Road, low block of Bedford St Se | 12:17 PM

Police responded with seven units to a report of a person with a gun on the low block of Bedford Street Southeast in the Prospect Park – East River Road neighborhood at 12:17 PM Saturday. The neighborhood saw an identical call type earlier this week when officers responded to a person-with-a-gun report on November 11.

· · ·

🔴 PERSON WITH WEAPON — Hawthorne, 1000 block of West Broadway | 5:33 PM

Six Minneapolis police units responded to a person-with-a-weapon call on the 1000 block of West Broadway in Hawthorne at 5:33 PM Friday. The call adds to a violent week in the neighborhood, which has logged two person-with-a-gun calls, four gunfire sensor activations, and a stabbing since November 7. Police reported a death on nearby Lowry Ave N late Wednesday night.

· · ·

🔴 GUNFIRE OVERNIGHT — 2 calls across 2 neighborhoods | 8:30 PM – 5:17 AM

The first ShotSpotter sensors lit up at 8:30 PM in East Phillips, where four squad cars rolled to the 1800 block of 28th Street East to investigate the gunfire alert. The neighborhood sat quiet after that, but the night was not over. Just before dawn at 5:17 AM, sensors picked up another activation in Hawthorne on the 2100 block of Emerson Avenue North, bringing a single unit to the scene. Hawthorne has shown up four times in the past week for gun-related calls, making it one of the busier areas in the city for this kind of activity. The two activations came nearly nine hours apart and on opposite ends of town, so a direct connection is unlikely, though in a city with active street violence it is never impossible for one incident to spark another somewhere else. By the time the sun came up, two neighborhoods had logged gunfire alerts overnight, but neither call led to a confirmed shooting dispatch with victims or crime scenes.

· · ·

🔴 ASSAULTS OVERNIGHT — 10 calls across 6 neighborhoods | 11:09 AM – 3:56 AM

Ten assault-in-progress calls came in over the past 17 hours across seven Minneapolis neighborhoods. Near North started the day at 11:09 a.m. with a two-unit response on Plymouth Avenue. Seward saw three calls total, two of them back-to-back at the same 27th Avenue South block just after 3:50 a.m. Willard-Hay drew the heaviest response of the night when seven units rolled to Golden Valley Road at 6:34 p.m. Downtown West logged two calls within half an hour around 2 a.m. on Hennepin and 5th Street, consistent with its place atop the 7-day assault count at 17 calls. The North Loop added two more between 2:45 and 3:52 a.m. on 2nd Street North.

· · ·

🔴 ROBBERIES OVERNIGHT — 3 calls across 3 neighborhoods | 11:00 AM – 1:17 AM

Three robberies hit Minneapolis overnight, spread across Ventura Village, Lind-Bohanon and Corcoran. The earliest came at 1:17 AM in Corcoran near 30th and 22nd Ave S, dispatched as a robbery of person with a single unit responding. Later that morning at 11:00 AM, Ventura Village saw a dwelling robbery report near 18th and Chicago Ave, also drawing one unit. The third call came at 2:45 PM in Lind-Bohanon near 51st and Dupont Ave N, this one pulling two units to a dwelling robbery report. All three were after-the-fact reports rather than in-progress calls. The 7-day context shows robbery activity scattered across six neighborhoods with no single area standing out, though Hawthorne, Downtown West and Central each logged two calls in the past week.

· · ·

🔴 BURGLARIES OVERNIGHT — 5 calls across 5 neighborhoods | 10:31 AM – 1:34 AM

Five burglary calls landed between 10:31 AM Saturday and 1:34 AM Sunday, with three hitting residences and two targeting businesses. The first came in at 10:31 AM when four units rolled to a business on University Avenue SE in Prospect Park. At 1:41 PM a single unit responded to a home break-in on Harriet Avenue in Whittier, a neighborhood that has logged four burglary calls over the past week. Four units answered another business break-in on Olson Memorial Highway in the North Loop at 9:32 PM. Two more residential calls followed overnight: four units to a home on 3rd Street NE in Bottineau at 11:05 PM, then a single-unit response to a dwelling on 13th Avenue S in Powderhorn Park at 1:34 AM.
